$comment: Notable liberties: where the kit departs from, reinterprets, or extends Apple's Human Interface Guidelines for the web. LIBERTIES.md is generated from this file: run `npm run catalog:docs`.

liberties.title: pt → px 1:1, then rem.
liberties.detail: A HIG point equals one CSS px at the device's scale factor. Evidence: Playwright 1.64.1 describes iPhone 17 Pro as 402 px wide @3× DPR, and Apple publishes 402 pt wide for that phone (⚠ the live HIG no longer lists device specs, so the pt figure comes from memory and is unverified). Sizes are then written in rem at a 16 px root. The CSS `pt` unit (1/72 in = 1.333 px) is **banned**, because it would turn 17 pt into 22.7 px.
liberties.rationale: Correct, testable translation. Stylelint `unit-disallowed-list: ["pt"]`.

liberties.title: Dynamic Type → rem plus browser text size and zoom.
liberties.detail: No web API exposes the iOS Dynamic Type category. Optional: WebKit's `font: -apple-system-body` on `html` reportedly tracks Dynamic Type in Safari, then the family is reset. ⚠ Not verified this pass; test on a device before adopting.
liberties.rationale: The nearest web mechanism.

liberties.title: One type scale (iOS "Large" defaults) for all widths.
liberties.detail: The macOS 13 pt body is too small for web reading. Two display sizes above Large Title are added for storefront heroes, using fluid `clamp()` with rem bounds and covered by the 200% zoom tests.
liberties.rationale: Storefront marketing needs bigger headings than HIG apps.

liberties.title: WCAG's definition of large text replaces HIG's table.
liberties.detail: HIG's contrast table gives 3:1 for bold text at any size and for 18 pt and up. WCAG's "large text" is ≥ 18 pt (24 px) regular or ≥ 14 pt (18.66 px) bold. So small bold text still needs 4.5:1. HIG's dark-mode "strive for 7:1" is adopted for primary and secondary text.
liberties.rationale: HIG's table is looser than the WCAG text it cites; WCAG is the legal and audit standard.

liberties.title: Targets: 44 px by default; HIG's 28 pt "minimum" is not used.
liberties.detail: WCAG's 24 px floor applies only to dense inline cases.
liberties.rationale: HIG's 28 pt minimum is below the comfortable touch size; 44 also equals WCAG 2.5.5 AAA.

liberties.title: Accessibility settings → media queries.
liberties.detail: Increase Contrast → `prefers-contrast: more` (Chrome 96 / Safari 14.1 / Firefox 101). Reduce Transparency → `prefers-reduced-transparency` (Chrome 118; **not** Safari; Firefox behind a flag), so opaque fallbacks also key off `prefers-contrast`. Bold Text has **no web equivalent** and is dropped. Windows `forced-colors` is added.
liberties.rationale: Browser support per BCD 8.1.8.

liberties.title: Liquid Glass → `backdrop-filter` material
liberties.detail: (blur + saturate over a role-tinted surface at a fixed opacity floor), with opaque fallbacks. No lensing, refraction, or specular highlights. `-webkit-backdrop-filter` is still emitted (BCD: unprefixed Safari 18; Chrome 76; Firefox 103).
liberties.rationale: Cheap, legible, and avoids imitating Apple trade dress (§3.1).

liberties.title: Safe areas → `env(safe-area-inset-*)`
liberties.detail: with `viewport-fit=cover` (Chrome 69 / Safari 11.1 / Firefox 65). Dynamic Island and camera housing are covered by the same insets.
liberties.rationale: Direct web equivalent.

liberties.title: Size classes → width breakpoints plus container queries
liberties.detail: (Chrome 105 / Safari 16 / Firefox 110). The vertical size class is approximated by a `max-height` query only for landscape phones.
liberties.rationale: The web has no size-class API.

liberties.title: System colors → our own palette
liberties.detail: under HIG-style semantic role names. Apple's measured values are not reused (system blue light is 3.52:1 on white). Our tertiary label meets 4.5:1, unlike HIG's low-alpha tertiary/quaternary; quaternary is reserved for disabled UI.
liberties.rationale: Accessibility and independence from Apple's values.

liberties.title: SF Symbols → Lucide
liberties.detail: (ISC + MIT). A stroke-width token stands in for symbol weights, and icons size in `em`.
liberties.rationale: License (§3.1).

liberties.title: One open font set everywhere; no San Francisco.
liberties.detail: Inter for UI and body text, Source Serif 4 for optional editorial headings, IBM Plex Mono for code and numbers. All are OFL-1.1 and in Shopify's font library. System-font keywords that would render SF Pro on Apple devices are not used either.
liberties.rationale: Owner decision (2026-11-03): zero licensing ambiguity (§3.1), and the same rendering on every platform, which keeps visual baselines deterministic.
liberties.note: Revised from the research report, which proposed SF Pro through system-font keywords with an Inter fallback.

liberties.title: Haptics and audio cues dropped.
liberties.detail: Feedback is visual plus a live region. Copy says "select", not "tap"/"click".
liberties.rationale: ⚠ Web Vibration support on iOS Safari not verified; HIG haptic patterns don't apply.

liberties.title: Platform-only guidance dropped:
liberties.detail: menu bar, Dock, windows/panels, widgets, Live Activities, complications, Digital Crown, Apple Pencil, Action button, Camera Control, tvOS focus engine and safe-area figures, visionOS spatial/ornaments, game controls, Siri/Shortcuts, App Clips, app icons (favicon/touch icon only), Spotlight, Quick Look.
liberties.rationale: Not applicable to responsive web storefronts.

liberties.title: Optional site appearance toggle,
liberties.detail: defaulting to System. HIG advises against app-specific appearance settings.
liberties.rationale: Some merchants require a brand-fixed theme. Allowed only when it defaults to System.

liberties.title: Submit stays enabled.
liberties.detail: HIG suggests enabling Next only once required data is present. Disabled buttons are not focusable and give no reason, so the kit validates on submit and focuses the first error.
liberties.rationale: Web a11y practice (WCAG 3.3.1/3.3.3).

liberties.title: Sentence case everywhere.
liberties.detail: HIG's Alerts page says button titles take sentence-style capitalisation, but Menus says menu items take title-style. The kit unifies on sentence case.
liberties.rationale: Consistency, as HIG Writing itself requires.

liberties.title: All controls are Tab-focusable.
liberties.detail: HIG's iPadOS keyboard note discourages keyboard navigation on buttons and switches, leaving that to Full Keyboard Access.
liberties.rationale: On the web, WCAG 2.1.1 requires it.

liberties.title: Dialog button order uses logical flex order,
liberties.detail: so it mirrors in RTL.
liberties.rationale: HIG gives physical (trailing) placement.

liberties.title: Tab bar → header navigation plus an optional compact bottom bar (≤ 5 items, ours).
liberties.detail: HIG's floating Liquid Glass tab bar is not replicated.
liberties.rationale: Storefront convention. The live Tab bars page gives no numeric limit, so 5 is ours.

liberties.title: Sheet detents → CSS bottom sheets
liberties.detail: with 50% / 90% `dvh` snap points via scroll-snap, plus a grabber.
liberties.rationale: Nearest web pattern.

liberties.title: Elevated dark surfaces are explicit tokens
liberties.detail: applied by components, not automatic.
liberties.rationale: The web has no automatic elevated trait.

liberties.title: Motion numbers are ours.
liberties.detail: HIG gives no durations; tokens are capped at 400 ms.
liberties.rationale: Needed for automated checks.

liberties.title: Readable width is ours:
liberties.detail: 66ch target / 75ch max. HIG mentions readable-width guides but gives no number.
liberties.rationale: Needed for automated checks.

liberties.title: Web and commerce extensions not in HIG:
liberties.detail: skip link, breadcrumbs, cookie/age-consent banners (legal, so exempt from MOD-09), performance budgets, Shopify Theme Store floors.
liberties.rationale: Web requirements.

liberties.title: Apple Pay rules constrain only our layout.
liberties.detail: Shopify's dynamic checkout renders the actual buttons.
liberties.rationale: We don't control those buttons.

liberties.title: Clay vocabulary, adapted:
liberties.detail: Clay's physical `LEFT`/`RIGHT` become logical `start`/`end` on the web. Clay's `PERCENT` subtracts padding *and* gaps; CSS % does not, so the web shim uses `calc()`. Clay has no wrap or grid, so `Cluster` and `Grid` are web-only primitives (§4.5).
liberties.rationale: Fidelity where natural, per the captain's intent.

liberties.title: HIG spacing advice (~12/24 pt) is a warning, not an error.
liberties.rationale: It is approximate in HIG itself.

liberties.title: Shopify Theme Store floors adopted
liberties.detail: (Lighthouse perf ≥ 60, a11y ≥ 90 average; contrast; 24 px targets), with stricter kit targets on top.
liberties.rationale: Client themes may later be listed.

liberties.title: Haptic "press" feel → a pressed visual state
liberties.detail: (scale ≤ 0.98 or a fill change), disabled under reduced motion.
liberties.rationale: Web substitute.
